summary:
Ícaro-9 es una experiencia de terror y ciencia ficción para el navegador, formada por dos juegos conectados. Turno Nocturno es un juego de supervivencia para un jugador, inspirado en FNAF. Sos el técnico nocturno de una nave y tenés que mantener los motores, el oxígeno y las luces funcionando de 00:00 a 06:00 mientras tres aliens acechan a bordo. Tiene cinco noches, minijuegos de reparación, voces por radio, varios finales y una misión extra en 3D en primera persona en Kepler-B. Escape es un juego multijugador cooperativo en 3D para 1 a 4 jugadores. La tripulación completa misiones en una nave grande mientras un monstruo controlado por la computadora la persigue. Los jugadores se esconden en armarios, aturden al monstruo con la linterna, reviven a sus compañeros, sellan fugas de oxígeno, usan bengalas y señuelos, y llegan a la cápsula de escape.

El proyecto convierte una idea simple en una experiencia completa que funciona en cualquier navegador sin instalar nada. Combina narrativa, trabajo en equipo y rejugabilidad con modificadores al azar, estadísticas y varios finales. Muestra hasta dónde se puede llegar con creatividad y herramientas web modernas: un juego completo hecho por un estudiante, que se juega y se comparte con un solo link.
details:
Ícaro-9 is a browser-based space-horror experience made of two connected games, built to make real NASA spaceflight science something players feel instead of just read.

WHAT IT DOES

• Turno Nocturno (single player): you are the night technician of a spaceship. From 00:00 to 06:00 you must keep oxygen, engines, power and lights running while three alien creatures roam the ship. Repair minigames are modeled on the ISS Environmental Control and Life Support System (ECLSS): oxygen generated by water electrolysis, water recycling, ventilation and hull protection against micrometeoroids and orbital debris. Five nights, voiced radio calls, multiple endings and a bonus 3D first-person mission, "Assault on Kepler-B", named after NASA's Kepler mission.

• Escape (co-op 3D, 1–4 players): the crew completes missions across a large ship while an AI-driven alien hunts them. Players hide in lockers, stun the creature with flashlights, revive teammates, seal oxygen leaks by closing valves before pressure drops, and reach the escape pod. Random round modifiers, flares, decoys and end-of-round stats make every match different.

• A "Real Science · NASA Data" panel explains each mechanic with the NASA source behind it, and a random NASA fact appears on every game-over screen.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

It turns life-support engineering, orbital debris and exoplanet science into survival decisions. Players learn why oxygen must be recycled on long missions or why shielding matters, because failing costs them the game. It runs in any browser, with no install, on low-end school computers too, so it is easy to share in classrooms with a single link.

TOOLS

HTML5, CSS and JavaScript; Three.js (WebGL) for 3D, post-processing and procedural textures; Web Audio API for procedurally synthesized music and sound effects; real-time multiplayer rooms; AI assistance for code (Claude by Anthropic) and AI text-to-speech for radio voices.

CREATIVITY

We mixed two genres, FNAF-style tension and co-op escape, in one shared universe. All graphics, textures and music are generated by code, with no external art assets.

FACTORS CONSIDERED

Scientific accuracy, accessibility (browser, keyboard or touch, Spanish UI), performance on modest hardware, replayability, and clearly labeling all AI-assisted content.
